extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and Scientific Review Officers (SRG members and assigned reviewers)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for NIH reviewers on evaluating grant applications, participating in Scientific Review Group (SRG) meetings, scoring, and producing written critiques in accordance with FOA-specific criteria and NIH policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the overall impact that a proposed project will likely have on the biomedical research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Role of first-level peer reviewers is to assess overall impact. The SRG discusses merits of proposed studies and submits a final impact score for each application. See 'First Level: Peer Review' and 'Scoring in First Level Peer Review' for additional context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate using FOA-established criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must evaluate applications using the criteria established in the notice of funding opportunity to which an application(s) was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specific review criteria and considerations contained in the FOA; additional guidance is available through standard reviewer guidance documents such as 'Peer Review Criteria and Considerations' and the consolidated list of reviewer documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and confidentiality adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are required to certify that they understand the rules of integrity and confidentiality in the peer review process and the consequences for not following these rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is required to participate in NIH review meetings. Reviewers should review the 'Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review' guidance and complete required attestations in IAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest (COI) identification and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must certify before and after review meetings that all conflicts of interest were identified and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declaring COI is mandatory; reviewers must use IAR to certify pre-meeting and post-meeting COI forms. See 'Managing Conflicts of Interest in NIH Peer Review of Grants and Contracts' for examples and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of required reviewer trainings
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH reviewers are required to take trainings in review integrity and bias awareness to participate in most NIH review meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete trainings such as 'Review Integrity and Bias Awareness Training' prior to serving on panels; completion may be required to access meeting materials or participate in reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of human subjects, vertebrate animals, and biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: SRG discussions will include any concerns with the use of human subjects, vertebrate animals, and/or biohazards within applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During meetings reviewers should raise and evaluate ethical, regulatory, and safety issues related to human subjects protections, animal welfare, and biohazard containment as part of the overall evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring procedures: preliminary ratings and final overall impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are typically given a preliminary rating as part of assigned reviewers’ initial evaluations; an application’s final rating or 'overall impact score' is determined by the entire review panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned reviewers provide initial/preliminary ratings; the full SRG discusses the application and the panel determines the final impact score. See 'Scoring in First Level Peer Review' and related scoring documents for numeric scales and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and content of written critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer critiques are part of the summary statement and an important source of feedback for what reviewers liked and didn’t like about their application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critiques should clearly explain strengths and weaknesses, justify scores, and provide constructive feedback. Use the 'Reviewer Critique Information' resources and submit/manage critiques via IAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Internet Assisted Review (IAR) procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must use IAR to view meeting materials, certify confidentiality and COI forms, access applications, and submit scores and critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tasks in IAR include: access meeting materials, fill out personal profile, certify pre-meeting COI, submit & manage critiques and scores, view other reviewers’ critiques, submit final scores, and certify post-meeting COI. Follow 'IAR for Reviewers Online Help' for step‑by‑step instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in SRG discussions and meeting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are brought together as a Scientific Review Group (SRG) to discuss the merits of the studies proposed and to submit final impact scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend and actively participate in SRG discussions; follow meeting roles and overview guidance. New reviewers are encouraged to watch mock study section videos (e.g., 'NIH Peer Review: "Live" Mock Study Section') to learn how applications are discussed.
